newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish markka stays firm against mark, below 2.97.
newsitem.headline: Finnish markka stays firm against mark, below 2.97.

text.p: Upward pressure hit the Finnish markka after the Helsinki close on Friday with DEM/FIM bids firming to below 2.965 in some instances.

With rates on Sunday showing DEM/FIM at 2.967 against Friday's close around 2.978, operators said the Bank of Finland may intervene early Monday, but added that there are probably political limits to its markka sales.
"If the (foreign) currency inflow continues again this week and they (Bank of Finland) take in, say 10 billion markka in foreign reserves, I think it might be a bit difficult to explain," said one.

One analyst said the nearly 16 billion markka increase in foreign reserves announced by the bank last Friday would only cover its interventions to last Monday, and its positions in forwards would not be revealed for some time.

That factor was behind estimates cited in Finnish media over the weekend that the central bank has actually accumulated closer to 30 billion markka in foreign currencies. Technically it can keep buying currency, but that raises political problems.

Speaking on condition of anonymity, analysts said on Sunday that sustained central bank intervention might prompt some of Finland's European Union partners to object to the markka's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) mid-rate as clearly too weak.
"I think everyone knows in Europe it is not a question of the bank trying to increase its foreign currency reserves," said one.
The markka's recent sharp gains have largely been attributed to overseas investors assuming the markka can track the Norwegian crown in gains against the German mark.
Accordingly, analysts noted it was not surprising that U.S. investors may take advantage of an empty Finnish market to bid the markka firmer and improve their bullish positions.

Market operators last week said the central bank had tended to be active with DEM/FIM around 2.975 -- an approximate floor if, as some believe, it is aiming for a 2.25 percent fluctuation band around the ERM mid-rate of 3.04.
But one analyst noted that the crucial level for DEM/FIM locally remains around 2.95, where many options positions are clustered.
If the markka strengthens to that level, that could trigger a snowball effect also within the local market, the analyst said. -- Sara Henley, Helsinki newsroom +35 89 6805 0247
